To my understanding, General anesthesia doesn't work because the end-of-death rules don't permit unconsciousness. That wouldn't apply to local anesthesia.

Specifically, Experiment Log 23 on SCP-3984 seems to present this information. I'm just gonna copy paste it.

Experiment Log 23

Date: 2026-02-07
Experimenter: Dr. Joyce Michaels
Subject: D-374A, a female Macaca mulatta or Rhesus macaque

Purpose: To confirm or deny the above assumption: that it is not possible to cause the brain to become unconscious.

Procedure: Over the course of 5 days, D-374A was injected with:

  • A mild sedative
  • A strong sedative
  • A mild local anaesthetic
  • A mild general anaesthetic
  • Class C amnestics

Results: D-374A responded positively to the mild sedative (dosage was insufficient to cause sleep), local and general anaesthetic and amnestics. D-374A had no response to the strong sedative — in fact no effect of the sedative was observed, despite the weak sedative showing a positive drowsiness response.

Note: Sedation, at least to the point of unconsciousness, is not an option for future experiments. This supports the above assumption. - Dr. Joyce Michaels

item.title: Nope.
item.content:encoded:
While I agree that 049 wouldn't fit for a Borderline PD diagnosis, neither for bipolar personality disorder for a very simple reason

It does not exist.

Long Term Depression
That would be chronic depression. And it is not, since it had a recent debut of symptoms.

and Bipolar Personality Disorder.
Non existent diagnosis

dialectical behavior therapy program with Dr. Isaac.
Which is a nice treatment for Borderline personality disorder but is inappropriate here because it, per definition, is delivered in a combination of group and individual therapy.

You still wanna go with a psychiatric formal diagnosis? Go for a severe major depressive episode and provide a cognitive-behavioral psychotherapy, that is the kind of therapist that would devise a therapeutic approach as described.

As for Bipolar Disorder: it is a mood disorder in which mood episodes can have an irritable (manic + depressive, or "mixed state", but irritable is a pretty appropiate sum on a day to day language) or depressive, or manic (related to elated / grandiose feeling, and a heightened level of activity). These episodes should last for SEVERAL DAYS (unusual) to months (usual), not the "day of fury" described.

Regarding my previous suggestion, irritability is a common symptom in male subjects that present a depressive episode early on.

Dr North: bad Boi, no give bad advice!

PS trust me I'm a psychiatrist.

+ show block
– hide block

Fair enough on the canon anesthesia thing, I didn't know it was a replicated mistake.

  • Chronic feelings of emptiness.
  • Unclear or shifting self-image
  • Anxiety

There's 50% of the population (lol). These are symptoms of Borderline/Bipolar, sure, but they are non-specific; like trying to propose a diagnosis for something based on headaches and fatigue. Could be a million things, all of which would include headaches and fatigue in the symptoms list. I'm not faulting you for this, just offering some expertise.

In my unbidden opinion, I'd say bipolar would be better, but still not accurate. Bipolars go through manic phases where they feel like they are, well, manic — on top of the world. They cycle between this and deep depressions where they will just shut down for days. I suppose we could be seeing the depressive phase of a bipolar 049 here, but we'd expect a serious and amphetamine-like 180° at some point for the diagnosis to stand. If I were consulted, I'd say it is just depressive disorder or generalized anxiety disorder.

Even in a post-death world, people still get shot, tumors occur, and augments need to be installed.

What I was getting at is that most surgical procedures, those following these injuries too, would be to prevent death or other serious sequelae. I'm not sure how much justification most procedures would carry in this world, especially given real world considerations of expense. You 're right; I think augmentation would remain.

As for the delicate handling of 049; I don't know what the answer is, but it's my main gripe. Feels like the tale has equivocated how the Foundation in-universe would approach 049 and how the community would want a classic character treated .

Hey, thank you for reading and offering feedback! My responses are below. :)

+ show block

Anesthesia- That is not something I'm 100% on, but it's a rule of the canon. According to Captain Kirby, anesthesia no longer works because… I don't know why. I wish I could give you a reason but I simply don't have one. I know a tale in EoD from S1 mentions this but I can't recall it by name at the moment.

I suppose even if local anesthesia did work, 049 would likely just do it on his own anyway out of pride.

—BP Disorder- I used some of my old college literature (which may or may not be out of date now, now that I give it some thought!) to frame his diagnosis. Here are the symptoms I picked out.

  • Chronic feelings of emptiness.
  • Unclear or shifting self-image
  • Anxiety

I've been told a few times that Bipolar Disorder fits better, and I'm contemplating changing it to this unless I find something better.—

I've changed it to Bipolar Personality Disorder based on your suggestions. Thank you! :D

Surgery- Even in a post-death world, people still get shot, tumors occur, and augments need to be installed. You're right, it's pretty kid-glovey, but that's really the best they can do given the situation. I am open to suggestion. :D

item.content:encoded:
I think the idea of 049 post-ΩK is an almost automatically successful idea, but I am in the minority here and slightly let down at the execution. I'm trying to temper my reaction considering maybe such a let-down is almost just as inevitable as the idea is good, given the giant ingredients at play here.

Nitpicks
– hide block

To me, the classic character has become a shell of itself and isn't interesting to me anymore. It's not that you've just shot him in the chest, it's that you've declawed him. His expertise is no longer the source of his effectiveness as a character, but is relegated to be a purely participatory act of pseudo-inclusion for his psychological disposition — something the Foundation containment staff and Ethics Committee perhaps shouldn't be concerned with. I also can't help but see the picture of 049 helping direct Foundation surgeons as unintentionally humorous. All in all, I guess I'd just rather not see the classic character this way. But that's probably the point of the tale.

I have some medical nitpicks that will be of no interest to you or anyone else:

  • I am confused as to why anesthesia doesn't work post-ΩK. It is either general or local; local works on the nerve cells and keeps them from telling your brain you are in pain. General depresses the control centers of the brain so that it can't care if the nerves are telling it that. I don't see how the end of mortality would render either of these mechanisms ineffective.
  • 049 is misdiagnosed as having Borderline Personality Disorder. Borderlines are labile in their personalities; extremely outgoing and then unapologetically hostile once you do something they don't approve of. They are also professionals at mind games and using manipulation to get what they want from others, most characteristically injuring themselves to that end. Their behavior continues to be attention-seeking throughout the disorder. I don't see that in this 049; he is not labile, simply steadily depressed, and he has a defeatist attitude by the end, not one that is attempting manipulation for its gain. Edit: I agree with Doctor North above and they are right; the above described behavior is commonly out of a fear of abandonment. Gesturing suicide is the usual tactic to get the attention they want.
  • I'm not sure why surgeons are still performing surgery post-death. Perhaps for symptomatic relief — from painful conditions comes to mind — but we've already been told that anesthetics don't work in this reality (fixing the previous nitpick would fix this one too). It's not clear to me how they could justify such kid-gloves for the psychological state of an anomaly that's historically dedicated to insensitivity for humanity, while apparently disregarding or putting to vote the pain that would accompany performing unnecessary surgery (no one is going to die from not doing the surgery) on fully-feeling and unavoidably waking people. I can't at present think of a procedure that would be worth it pain-wise in this scenario. Edit: Maybe amputation or plastic surgery. But I don't think you'd need a 049 consult for those (certainly not the plastics!).

Novote for now but I'll come back to it, because it really is such a great combo of ingredients.

I have a minor suggestion for the last sentence of the last paragraph of the containment procedures:

Weekly visits from a Level-3 approved psychiatrist have been scheduled on a weekly basis.

The double-usage of the word "weekly" at the end is kind of redundant, and I would recommend trimming it to just read:

"Weekly visits from a Level-3 approved psychiatrist have been scheduled."

The following bit seems to stem from the original article:

+ The building fronts are just fronts
- For the people watching

ceramic mask

I don't think those masks were actually made of ceramic. I tried looking it up, but it's kind of hard to find (it's easy to find what the rest of the outfit was made from), but I think the mask was leather, too. I'm admittedly not certain about that. And apparently the outfit is anachronistic here, at least according to its self-proclaimed origin date, since it wasn't invented until the early 17th century.

Actually, now that I'm really looking at it, that mask in the picture doesn't even look like a legitimate plague doctor's mask. It looks like a Carnivale mask based off the plague doctors. I don't think it covers the lower half of his face, and the eyes should have glass lenses. I know this is one of the most iconic images on the site, I don't expect or even want it to be changed, just sayin'…

Anyway, these two whopping issues are minor things and didn't stop me from enjoying this +1. Thank you for writing it!
